newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Eskom hikes prices by 5 pct from 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Eskom hikes prices by 5 pct from 1997.

text.p: South Africa's electricity parastatal Eskom said on Thursday that the average price of electricity would be raised by five percent from January 1, 1997 and could be reviewed later in the year.
John Maree, chairman of the electricity council, said a further price adjustment could be called for due to the uncertainty in the electricity supply sector.

"We estimate that consumer price inflation will average approximately 8.5 percent in 1997 so our five percent increase will give our customers a price reduction in real terms of 3.5 percent," Maree said.

"However, recognising considerable uncertainty that exists within the electricity supply industry, a further price adjustment may be considered in 1997 if a new financial framework so requires," he added.

Maree said Eskom had consistently reduced the real price of electricity over the past 10 years by 68 percent in a bid to be the world's lowest-cost producer of electricity and make electricity affordable to a larger number of people in the country.

Eskom was also committed to reducing prices in real terms by 15 percent between 1995 and the year 2000, Maree said. He said this would be taking place amid uncertainty over, among others, the possibility of the industry becoming a tax and dividend paying entity.
